Saturated model

Source: R/models.R
saturated.Rd

The model with no assumption on the dependence between the tests: the distribution of the profiles is free within each disease class. It is written in a transparent parametrization, which separates the identified parameters from the non-identified ones:

  • identified: the frequency of each response profile, the verification probability of each profile with at least one verified subject, and the proportion of diseased among its verified subjects;

  • not identified: the proportion of diseased among the unverified subjects of each such profile, which is fixed by the verification mechanism, and the proportion of diseased in each never-verified profile, whose posterior equals its prior.

Usage

saturated(
  frequency_prior = prior_dirichlet(1),
  verified_prior = prior_beta(0.5, 2),
  profile_prevalence_prior = prior_beta(0.5, 2),
  unverified_prevalence_prior = NULL,
  verification = mar()
)

Arguments

frequency_prior

prior_dirichlet() on the vector of profile frequencies \(\omega = (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_J)\). Its concentration is a single positive number, the same for every profile, or a vector with one positive value per profile, in binary order: the profile with all tests negative comes first, and the first test changes fastest (with two tests: (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1)). Default prior_dirichlet(1), the uniform distribution on the simplex.

verified_prior

Prior on the verification probability \(v_t\) of each profile with at least one verified subject. The same prior is used, independently, for each such profile. A prior on a probability, such as prior_beta() or elicit_beta(), acts on \(v_t\) itself; a prior on the real line, such as prior_normal() or prior_student(), acts on \(\mathrm{logit}\,v_t\). Default prior_beta(0.5, 2), the uniform distribution on (0, 1). Never-verified profiles have no such parameter.

profile_prevalence_prior

Prior on \(\phi^{(1)}_t\), the proportion of diseased among the verified subjects of each profile with at least one verified subject. The same prior is used, independently, for each such profile, with the same rules as verified_prior: a prior on a probability acts on the proportion, a prior on the real line on its logit. Default prior_beta(0.5, 2), the uniform distribution on (0, 1).

unverified_prevalence_prior

Prior on \(q_t\), the proportion of diseased in each never-verified profile (a profile with no verified subject). It has no default prior: its default NULL means that no prior is given. It is required when at least one profile is never verified, and baysesp() stops with an error if it is missing in that case. Its value can be one prior, which applies to every never-verified profile, or a list with one prior per never-verified profile, in binary order among those profiles (with two tests, if both (0,1) and (1,1) are never verified, the list has two elements: the first for (0,1), the second for (1,1)). A list of length one is the same as a single prior. Each prior has the same allowed classes as verified_prior. Its posterior equals its prior, so it is an explicit assumption; use elicit_beta() to specify it from a plausible value and an upper bound.

verification

Verification mechanism: mar() (the default), where verification depends only on the test results, or mnar(), where it also depends on the disease status. See Details for what changes.

Value

An object of class saturated.

Details

With \(K\) tests there are \(J = 2^K\) response profiles \(t\). For each profile the model has four parameters:

  • \(\omega_t = P(T = t)\): frequency of the profile among all subjects;

  • \(v_t = P(V = 1 \mid T = t)\): probability that a subject with profile \(t\) is verified;

  • \(\phi^{(1)}_t = P(D = 1 \mid T = t, V = 1)\): proportion of diseased among the verified subjects with profile \(t\);

  • \(\phi^{(0)}_t = P(D = 1 \mid T = t, V = 0)\): proportion of diseased among the unverified subjects with profile \(t\).

Let \(n_{t,1}\) and \(n_{t,0}\) be the numbers of verified diseased and verified healthy subjects with profile \(t\), \(u_t\) the number of unverified subjects, and \(N_t = n_{t,1} + n_{t,0} + u_t\). The log-likelihood is $$\ell = \sum_t \Big[N_t \log \omega_t + (n_{t,1} + n_{t,0}) \log v_t + u_t \log(1 - v_t) + n_{t,1} \log \phi^{(1)}_t + n_{t,0} \log(1 - \phi^{(1)}_t)\Big].$$ The unverified subjects enter only through \(N_t\) and \(u_t\), because their disease status is not observed. The proportion \(\phi^{(0)}_t\) does not enter the log-likelihood: the data carry no information on it, so it is determined by the verification mechanism and by \(\phi^{(1)}_t\). A never-verified profile has no verified subject, so \(v_t = 0\) and only its first term remains.

With verification = mar() (missing at random) verification depends only on the test results: among subjects with the same profile, verified and unverified subjects have the same proportion of diseased, so \(\phi^{(0)}_t = \phi^{(1)}_t\).

With verification = mnar() (missing not at random) verification may also depend on the disease status: $$\mathrm{logit}\,\phi^{(0)}_t = \mathrm{logit}\,\phi^{(1)}_t - \beta,$$ where \(\beta\) is the log odds ratio of verification between diseased and healthy subjects with the same profile. Equivalently, \(\exp(-\beta)\) is the odds ratio of disease between unverified and verified subjects with the same profile: \(\beta > 0\) means that the unverified are less often diseased. There is one \(\beta\) common to all profiles with verified subjects, or one per profile with verification = mnar(by_profile = TRUE). Since \(\beta\) does not enter the log-likelihood, its posterior equals its prior, and the results depend on the assumed value: they should be examined over a range of plausible values.

The quantities of interest are obtained as follows. For each profile, $$\psi_t = v_t \phi^{(1)}_t + (1 - v_t) \phi^{(0)}_t$$ is the proportion of diseased among subjects with profile \(t\); for a never-verified profile \(\phi^{(0)}_t = q_t\) is the proportion of diseased in it, so \(\psi_t = q_t\). Then $$\pi = \sum_t \omega_t \psi_t, \qquad \theta_{1,t} = \frac{\omega_t \psi_t}{\pi}, \qquad \theta_{0,t} = \frac{\omega_t (1 - \psi_t)}{1 - \pi},$$ where \(\pi\) is the prevalence, \(\theta_{1,t} = P(T = t \mid D = 1)\) and \(\theta_{0,t} = P(T = t \mid D = 0)\). The sensitivity of a test is the sum of \(\theta_{1,t}\) over the profiles with a positive result for that test, and its specificity the sum of \(\theta_{0,t}\) over the profiles with a negative result. Under both mechanisms the never-verified profiles enter \(\pi\) through \(q_t\), whose posterior equals its prior.

Examples

saturated()
#> <saturated> saturated model, transparent parametrization
#>   frequency_prior:             Dirichlet(concentration = 1)
#>   verified_prior:              Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   profile_prevalence_prior:    Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   unverified_prevalence_prior: none
#>   verification:                mar
saturated(unverified_prevalence_prior = elicit_beta(mean = 0.005, upper = 0.015))
#> <saturated> saturated model, transparent parametrization
#>   frequency_prior:             Dirichlet(concentration = 1)
#>   verified_prior:              Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   profile_prevalence_prior:    Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   unverified_prevalence_prior: Beta(mean = 0.005, precision = 197.8)
#>   verification:                mar
saturated(verification = mnar())
#> <saturated> saturated model, transparent parametrization
#>   frequency_prior:             Dirichlet(concentration = 1)
#>   verified_prior:              Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   profile_prevalence_prior:    Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   unverified_prevalence_prior: none
#>   verification:                mnar
